questions.prompt: Should one ReleaseCandidate bind the exact source commit/tree, approved project baselines, package version, release configuration, toolchain identities, and EnvironmentReadinessReceipt? Recommended: yes.

Should ReleasePreparation be one conditional semantic module after SystemVerification, with a separate ReleaseVerificationGate deciding candidate readiness before BusinessAcceptance? Recommended: yes.

Should the required candidate set contain a deterministic installable tarball, release catalog/manifest, CycloneDX SBOM, SHA-256 ledger, release notes, license/notice material, and a compact evidence index? Recommended: yes.

Should RP-001 own preparation and verification of an exact release candidate only, while publication, deployment, protected-main promotion, and release approval remain outside its authority? Recommended: yes.

Should ReleaseVerification require static verification, the complete deterministic test suite, package/export enumeration, isolated install/import checks, SBOM and checksum verification, documentation/link checks, secret scanning, and a clean Windows Desktop consumer run? Recommended: yes.

Should evidence preserve exact commands, tool/adapter versions, configuration and input digests, exit codes, durations, stdout/stderr or artifact digests, candidate bytes, and checkpoint identities? Recommended: yes.

Should the successful Gate output be a ReleaseReadinessBaseline/record that authorizes only downstream human-controlled publication consideration and never performs publication or branch/tag mutation? Recommended: yes.

Should candidate materialization checkpoint exact prepared outputs before any merge or external effect, with exact replay performing zero packaging, download, signing, upload, tagging, or publication calls? Recommended: yes.

Should release execution be offline by default, allow only exact destination/purpose network grants, reject secret-bearing artifacts or logs, and require checksum-pinned project-local tools? Recommended: yes.

Should V1 ship deterministic native Node/Windows implementations for cataloging, packing, checksum/SBOM validation, and installed-package verification, with hosted release systems represented only by optional bounded adapters? Recommended: yes.

Should deterministic byte equality, fail-closed validation, zero-call replay, crash recovery, redaction, isolated clean-install verification, and honest adapter maturity be mandatory release acceptance properties? Recommended: yes.

Should Desktop present one compact candidate/readiness summary containing blockers, warnings, version/source identity, artifact digests, verification coverage, and direct evidence links? Recommended: yes.
Should any source, configuration, version, tool, baseline, or environment drift create a new immutable candidate attempt instead of updating historical candidate evidence? Recommended: yes.
Should RP-001 require an accepted current EnvironmentReadinessReceipt before candidate materialization and revalidate it before every effectful release step? Recommended: yes.

Should source archives generated by GitHub remain externally produced publication artifacts, while RP-001 verifies their expected source identity but never predicts or self-certifies their final bytes? Recommended: yes.

Should RP-001 cover GitHub source plus an installable library tarball for ChatGPT/Codex Desktop on Windows, while public npm, one-click Desktop installation, hosted operation, and non-Windows claims remain excluded? Recommended: yes.

Should every verification family be required unless ReleaseVerificationGate records an explicit policy-backed ApprovedNotApplicable disposition, with failed, missing, stale, or unknown required evidence blocking readiness? Recommended: yes.

Should trusted contributors project only forward factual links from approved source and environment state through candidate artifacts and verification evidence, while adapters receive no graph access? Recommended: yes.

Should version selection, changelog approval, prerelease versus stable designation, and final publication approval remain explicit owner decisions rather than adapter- or Core-inferred values? Recommended: yes.
Should verification re-load candidate bytes from content-addressed storage and reject rebuilt, substituted, partially retrieved, or digest-mismatched artifacts? Recommended: yes.
Should RP-001 fail closed on dependency, action-pin, license, provenance, SBOM, checksum, signature/attestation, or secret-scan findings according to one versioned release policy? Recommended: yes.

Should adapter slots be capability-oriented—materialize, inspect, verify, attest, and publication-prerequisite probe—with no product-specific routing in Generic Core and no silent fallback? Recommended: yes.

Should V1 record materialization and verification duration, cache hits, retries, artifact sizes, and bottlenecks without imposing a universal wall-clock SLA until Windows reference-host measurements establish one? Recommended: yes.
Should all proposed network, signing, credential, filesystem, process, tag, or remote-repository effects be consolidated and shown for explicit approval before execution? Recommended: yes.
